reason: This text fragment from Exodus 1 describes Pharaoh's command to the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn boys, the midwives' fear of God (יִרְאוּ אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים), their disobedience to Pharaoh's command, and God's subsequent blessing upon them ('וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹת'). The passage contains no indication of improper worship, nor does it depict Yahweh's anger. Rather, it demonstrates God rewarding those who fear him with protection and blessing. The narrative focuses on divine protection of the Hebrew people from persecution, not divine punishment for religious transgressions.
